# MLS-Bench: llm-early-exit-criterion

# Self-Speculative Drafting for an Early-Exit Decoder

## Research Question

This is the early-exit question asked where early-exit models are actually used.
A decoder trained so that its intermediate layers can emit tokens has to decide
at which layer a token may exit and when. In self-speculative decoding that
decision is the draft: the exit layer (or set of layers) that proposes tokens,
and the moment drafting stops. The model drafts for itself: a subset of its own layers, followed by the shared final norm and LM
head, proposes the next few tokens, and the full model verifies all of them in
one parallel pass. The longest drafted prefix that agrees with the full model's
greedy choice is kept, plus one token from the full model, so the output is
exactly the full model's greedy decoding. Only the cost changes, so a wrong exit
costs compute instead of quality. A shallow
draft is cheap but often wrong; a deep draft is right but costs nearly as much as
the full model; drafting many tokens pays off only when most of them are
accepted. **Which layers should draft, how many tokens should be drafted, and
when should drafting stop, round by round, to generate the most tokens per unit
of decoder compute?**

## Background

Early exit was first posed as a per-token confidence decision with a quality
loss: CALM (Schuster et al., NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2207.07061) exits when a softmax
margin, a hidden-state saturation measure or a learned classifier is confident
enough. LayerSkip (Elhoushi et al., *LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and
Self-Speculative Decoding*, ACL 2024, arXiv:2404.16710) trains models so that
every layer can exit (layer dropout plus an early-exit loss on the shared head).
It then uses the exit for lossless self-speculation, drafting with a fixed exit
layer and a fixed number of tokens per round. The same per-token confidence
signals reappear here as the rule that stops drafting. The
optimal exit layer and draft length vary with the task and within one generation.
The methods below make them adaptive in different ways. Some change the draft
length from acceptance feedback or from the draft's own confidence. Some pick the
exit layer online from statistics of every layer's prediction at the verified
positions. Others search over arbitrary sets of attention and MLP sublayers to
skip, or verify a token tree instead of a chain.

This task is about self-speculation, where the model is its own drafter. It does
not train or use a separate draft model or draft heads.

## What You Can Modify

`layerskip-ee-lab/mlsee/draft_policy.py`, the editable region only (between the
`BEGIN EDITABLE REGION` / `END EDITABLE REGION` markers). It defines the
controller. The controller runs in one persistent, unprivileged process that is
not given a GPU:

```python
def calibrate(cal, n_layers, seed, simulate) -> dict      # once, before decoding
def begin(prompt, state) -> None                           # a new prompt
def plan(state, ops) -> dict                               # the next round's draft
def step(feat, state) -> bool                              # keep drafting?
def tree(steps, state) -> (parent, token)                  # optional token tree
def observe(result, state) -> None                         # verification outcome
```

* `plan` returns either `{"exit": E}` (draft with layers `0..E-1`) or
  `{"mask": m}`. The mask has 2L booleans: entry `2l` is layer `l`'s attention
  sublayer and entry `2l+1` its MLP sublayer, and at least one must be kept. The
  same dict carries `max_draft` (tokens to draft this round), `feedback` (call
  `step` after each draft token), `tree` (call `tree` after drafting and verify a
  tree) and `keep_states` (keep sublayer states for `ops.states`).
* `step` receives the draft head's top-k logits and log-partition for the token
  just drafted.
* `tree` receives the draft distributions of the drafted steps. It returns a node
  list where each parent comes before its children (`-1` = child of the last
  committed token). A node at depth k must be one of the top-k tokens of draft
  step k-1.
* `begin` receives every layer's top-k logits and log-partition at the last
  prompt positions, those prompt tokens, and the first generated token. `observe`
  receives the number of drafted tokens accepted, the committed tokens, the full
  model's greedy token at each verified position, and every layer's top-k at
  the verified positions (the "shadow" predictions).
* `ops`, inside `plan` only, offers four calls:
  * `ops.probe(mask, i0, i1)` runs a candidate draft over already-generated
    tokens `[i0, i1)` of the current prompt.
  * `ops.apply(block, x, n)` applies one sublayer to states you supply.
  * `ops.states(n)` returns the sublayer-boundary states of the last `n`
    committed tokens.
  * `ops.head(x)` applies the final norm and LM head.
* `calibrate` receives `cal` (layer count, hidden size, per-sublayer costs,
  limits) and `simulate(state)`. Each `simulate` call runs the real decoder with
  this controller on a few calibration prompts and returns the realised eTPL.
  It is limited to `cal["max_simulations"]` calls.

**Cost.** Decoding is memory-bound, so a pass costs the decoder parameters it
loads. One unit is one decoder layer. An attention sublayer costs its share of a
layer's parameters and the MLP sublayer costs the rest (`cal["sublayer_cost"]`).
The costs are:

| what | cost |
|---|---|
| a draft step | the sublayers it runs |
| a verification, however many tokens or tree nodes | all L layers |
| `ops.probe` | the sublayers it runs, once |
| `ops.apply` | its sublayer, once |
| the prompt's prefill (yields the first token) | L |

The embedding and LM head are not counted. Every emitted token is the full
model's greedy choice, computed and checked by the decoder, so no controller can
change the text.

`numpy` and the standard library are available, and so is `bayes_opt`
(bayesian-optimization 1.5.1). torch imports, but the controller process is not
given a GPU. The vendored LayerSkip sources under `/workspace/layerskip-ee-lab/`
are readable reference, including the released self-speculative decoding in
`self_speculation/`. There is no network. `draft_policy.py` must stay under
32768 bytes. All functions must be deterministic given `seed`.

## Fixed Pipeline

Everything outside the controller is fixed by the harness: the decoder that runs
drafts, verifications and the metered services, the cost accounting, and the

## Evaluation

Reported per setting:

| metric | meaning | direction |
|---|---|---|
| `etpl` | generated tokens per unit of decoder cost, per prompt, averaged over prompts | higher is better (scored) |
| `speedup_layers` | `etpl` divided by plain decoding's (1/L) | reported |

## Reference Baselines

* `default` (the unmodified starter): LayerSkip's released self-speculative
  decoding, with a fixed exit layer and a fixed draft length (E = 3, 6 tokens).
  Source: `self_speculation/self_speculation_generator.py`, arXiv:2404.16710.
* `fs`: a finite-state draft length that grows by one after a fully accepted
  round and shrinks by one otherwise. This is the FS baseline of DEL
  (arXiv:2504.05598), ported from its released code.
* `dv`: Draft & Verify's adaptive draft-exiting (Zhang et al., ACL 2024,
  arXiv:2309.08168). Drafting stops below a confidence threshold that is moved
  to hold a target acceptance rate. Ported from DEL's released DV baseline.
* `del`: DEL (Entezari Zarch et al., *Context-Aware Dynamic Exit Layer for
  Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding*, COLM 2025, arXiv:2504.05598). It tracks
  every layer's acceptance rate from the shadow predictions, picks the exit layer
  that maximises expected tokens per loaded layer, and stops drafting by a
  per-layer confidence threshold. Ported from the released code.
* `swift`: SWIFT (Xia et al., *SWIFT: On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding for
  LLM Inference Acceleration*, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.06916). It searches online
  over which attention and MLP sublayers to skip (random and Bayesian search,
  scored by parallel drafting on the generated context) and verifies a
  confidence-aware token tree. Ported from the released code.
* `knapspec`: KnapSpec (Cha et al., *Self-Speculative Decoding via Adaptive
  Layer Selection as a Knapsack Problem*, ICML 2026). A dynamic programme over
  attention and MLP sublayers trades hidden-state fidelity against each
  sublayer's cost, re-optimised periodically. Ported from the released code.
* `random_exit`: a null that draws a random exit layer every round with the
  starter's draft length.

  with the last layer's token (the verified token);

  mismatched shadow tokens and EMA counts of matches / mismatches;
  tau_l = mean confidence of matched and mismatched;

  0..gamma_max-1; cost (L - (l+1)) + (g+1)(l+1); argmax of their ratio;

first token, so the reference's first round (one token drafted at E = 1 while
the prompt is prefilled) is replaced by statistics from the same 32 prompt
positions and the first planned round already uses the selected (E, gamma).

convention.

OMEGA = 0.95
D_MAX = 18


def calibrate(cal, n_layers, seed, simulate):
    return {"L": int(n_layers)}


def _probs(val, lse):
    """Probability of each layer's greedy token: (rows, positions)."""
    return np.exp(np.asarray(val[..., 0], dtype=np.float64) - np.asarray(lse, dtype=np.float64))


def _update(state, sid, sval, slse, context=False):
    """DEL.update_acceptance_and_confidence_stats with the shadow table of
    shape (L, positions): rows 0..L-2 = eligible layers, row L-1 = target."""
    L = state["L"]
    toks = np.asarray(sid[..., 0])
    conf = _probs(sval, slse)[:-1]
    match = toks[:-1] == toks[-1][None, :]
    if not context and state["gamma"] > 0:
        row = state["exit"] - 1                     # exit_layer - 1 - eligible[0]
        bad = np.nonzero(~match[row])[0]
        if bad.size:
            k = int(bad[0]) + 1
            match, conf = match[:, :k], conf[:, :k]
    t_conf = (conf * match).sum(1)
    f_conf = (conf * ~match).sum(1)
    state["conf_sums"][:L - 1] = OMEGA * state["conf_sums"][:L - 1] + np.stack([t_conf, f_conf], 1)
    t = match.sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    state["counts"][:L - 1] = OMEGA * state["counts"][:L - 1] + np.stack([t, match.shape[1] - t], 1)

    L = state["L"]
    c = state["counts"][:L - 1]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        probs = c[:, 0] / c.sum(1)
    probs = np.where(np.isnan(probs), -np.inf, probs)
    gp = np.zeros((L - 1, GAMMA_MAX))
    for i in range(GAMMA_MAX):

MAX_APPLY_ROWS = 8192


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ framing
def write_frame(fd, header, arrays=None):
    arrays = arrays or {}
    names = sorted(arrays)
    meta = {"h": header, "a": [[n, str(arrays[n].dtype), list(arrays[n].shape)] for n in names]}
    hb = json.dumps(meta).encode()
    parts = [struct.pack("<Q", len(hb)), hb]
    for n in names:
        parts.append(np.ascontiguousarray(arrays[n]).tobytes())
    view = memoryview(b"".join(parts))
    while view:
        k = os.write(fd, view)
        view = view[k:]


def _read_exact(fd, n, deadline, alive=None):
    buf = bytearray()
    while len(buf) < n:
        left = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if left <= 0:
            raise TimeoutError("draft controller did not answer in time")
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], min(left, 1.0))
        if not r:
            if alive is not None:
                alive()
            continue
        chunk = os.read(fd, min(n - len(buf), 1 << 20))
        if not chunk:
            raise EOFError("draft controller closed its pipe")
        buf.extend(chunk)
    return bytes(buf)


_ALLOWED_DTYPES = {"bool", "uint8", "int32", "int64", "float16", "float32", "float64"}


def read_frame(fd, deadline, max_header=1 << 16, max_bytes=1 << 28, alive=None):
    (hl,) = struct.unpack("<Q", _read_exact(fd, 8, deadline, alive))
    if hl > max_header:
        raise ValueError("oversized frame header from the draft controller")
    meta = json.loads(_read_exact(fd, hl, deadline, alive))
    arrays = {}
    total = 0
    for name, dt, shape in meta.get("a", []):
        if dt not in _ALLOWED_DTYPES:
            raise ValueError("dtype %r not allowed in the protocol" % dt)
        if not isinstance(shape, list) or len(shape) > 4 or any(
                (not isinstance(s, int)) or s < 0 for s in shape):
            raise ValueError("bad array shape in the protocol")
        dt = np.dtype(dt)
        n = int(np.prod(shape)) * dt.itemsize
        total += n
        if total > max_bytes:
            raise ValueError("oversized frame from the draft controller")
        arrays[name] = np.frombuffer(_read_exact(fd, n, deadline, alive), dtype=dt).reshape(shape)
    if not isinstance(meta.get("h"), dict):
        raise ValueError("malformed frame header")
    return meta["h"], arrays


class RuleClient:
    """This process's side of the channel to the unprivileged controller process.

    Two FIFOs in the controller's work dir; the controller process gets no
    inherited descriptors (under Harbor it is started by the verifier's
    ``$MLSBENCH_RUN_UNTRUSTED`` helper)."""

    def __init__(self, argv, workdir, stderr_path, env, call_timeout, open_timeout=600.0):
        self.to_rule = os.path.join(workdir, "to_rule.fifo")
        self.from_rule = os.path.join(workdir, "from_rule.fifo")
        for f in (self.to_rule, self.from_rule):
            if os.path.lexists(f):
                os.unlink(f)
            os.mkfifo(f, 0o666)
            os.chmod(f, 0o666)
        self.rfd = os.open(self.from_rule, os.O_RDWR)
        self.err = open(stderr_path, "wb")
        self.p = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=self.err,
                                  stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=env, close_fds=True)
        self.call_timeout = call_timeout
        self.rc = None
        deadline = time.monotonic() + open_timeout
        while True:
            try:
                self.wfd = os.open(self.to_rule, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_NONBLOCK)
                break
            except OSError:
                if self.p.poll() is not None or time.monotonic() > deadline:
                    raise EOFError("draft controller process did not open its channel")
                time.sleep(0.05)
        os.set_blocking(self.wfd, True)

    def _check_alive(self):
        if self.p.poll() is not None:
            raise EOFError("draft controller process exited (rc %s)" % self.p.returncode)

    def send(self, header, arrays=None):
        write_frame(self.wfd, header, arrays)

    def recv(self, timeout=None):
        return read_frame(self.rfd, time.monotonic() + (timeout or self.call_timeout),
                          alive=self._check_alive)

    def close(self):
        try:
            os.close(self.wfd)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self.rc = self.p.wait(timeout=120)
        except Exception:
            self.p.kill()
            self.rc = self.p.wait()
        try:
            os.close(self.rfd)
        except Exception:
            pass
        self.err.close()


class ProtocolError(RuntimeError):
    pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ engine
class Engine:
    """The decoder stack run sublayer by sublayer over a preallocated KV cache.

    Sublayer b = 2*l is layer l's attention block (input norm, self-attention,
    residual add), b = 2*l + 1 its MLP block (post-attention norm, MLP, residual
    add).  The math is the HF Llama decoder layer's (same modules, same
    rotary embedding, same repeat_kv + SDPA)."""

    def __init__(self, model, cap):
        from transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama import apply_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
        self._rot, self._rep = apply_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
        self.m = model
        self.layers = model.model.layers
        self.L = len(self.layers)
        self.norm = model.model.norm
        self.head = model.lm_head
        self.emb = model.model.embed_tokens
        self.rotary = model.model.rotary_emb
        a0 = self.layers[0].self_attn
        self.nkv, self.hd = a0.num_key_value_heads, a0.head_dim
        self.nh, self.groups = a0.num_heads, a0.num_key_value_groups
        self.dtype = model.dtype
        dev = "cuda"
        self.K = torch.zeros((self.L, 1, self.nkv, cap, self.hd), dtype=self.dtype, device=dev)
        self.V = torch.zeros_like(self.K)
        self.cap = cap
        p_attn = sum(p.numel() for p in self.layers[0].self_attn.parameters()) \
            + sum(p.numel() for p in self.layers[0].input_layernorm.parameters())
        p_mlp = sum(p.numel() for p in self.layers[0].mlp.parameters()) \
            + sum(p.numel() for p in self.layers[0].post_attention_layernorm.parameters())
        self.c_attn = p_attn / float(p_attn + p_mlp)
        self.c_mlp = p_mlp / float(p_attn + p_mlp)
        self.sub_cost = np.asarray([self.c_attn, self.c_mlp] * self.L, dtype=np.float64)

    def rope(self, h, pos):
        return self.rotary(h, pos.view(1, -1))

    def attn(self, l, h, cs, ctx, write_at, qmask):
        """h: (1, q, d).  Keys = this layer's cached slots [0, ctx) + the q new
        tokens.  qmask: (q, q) bool, which new tokens each new token sees (None =
        causal).  write_at: slot index where the new K/V are stored (None = not
        stored)."""
        at = self.layers[l].self_attn
        x = self.layers[l].input_layernorm(h)
        q = x.shape[1]
        qs = at.q_proj(x).view(1, q, self.nh, self.hd).transpose(1, 2)
        ks = at.k_proj(x).view(1, q, self.nkv, self.hd).transpose(1, 2)
        vs = at.v_proj(x).view(1, q, self.nkv, self.hd).transpose(1, 2)
        cos, sin = cs
        qs, ks = self._rot(qs, ks, cos, sin)
        if write_at is not None:
            self.K[l, :, :, write_at:write_at + q] = ks
            self.V[l, :, :, write_at:write_at + q] = vs
            if write_at == ctx:
                kk, vv = self.K[l, :, :, :ctx + q], self.V[l, :, :, :ctx + q]
            else:
                kk = torch.cat([self.K[l, :, :, :ctx], ks], 2)
                vv = torch.cat([self.V[l, :, :, :ctx], vs], 2)
        else:
            kk = torch.cat([self.K[l, :, :, :ctx], ks], 2)
            vv = torch.cat([self.V[l, :, :, :ctx], vs], 2)
        kk, vv = self._rep(kk, self.groups), self._rep(vv, self.groups)
        if q == 1 and qmask is None:
            mask = None
        else:
            allow = torch.ones((q, ctx + q), dtype=torch.bool, device=h.device)
            allow[:, ctx:] = qmask if qmask is not None else torch.tril(
                torch.ones((q, q), dtype=torch.bool, device=h.device))
            mask = torch.zeros((1, 1, q, ctx + q), dtype=h.dtype, device=h.device)
            mask.masked_fill_(~allow, torch.finfo(h.dtype).min)
            qs, kk, vv = qs.contiguous(), kk.contiguous(), vv.contiguous()
        o = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(qs, kk, vv, attn_mask=mask, dropout_p=0.0)
        o = o.transpose(1, 2).reshape(1, q, self.nh * self.hd)
        return h + at.o_proj(o)

    def mlp(self, l, h):
        lay = self.layers[l]
        return h + lay.mlp(lay.post_attention_layernorm(h))

    def logits(self, h):
        return self.head(self.norm(h)).float()

    def run(self, h, pos, keep, ctx, write_at, qmask=None, collect=False):
        """Run the sublayers flagged in keep (bool[2L]) over h (1, q, d).  With
        collect, returns the 2L+1 sublayer-boundary states (list of (1, q, d))."""
        cs = self.rope(h, pos)
        states = [h] if collect else None
        for b in range(2 * self.L):
            l = b // 2
            if keep[b]:
                h = self.attn(l, h, cs, ctx, write_at, qmask) if b % 2 == 0 else self.mlp(l, h)
            if collect:
                states.append(h)
        return h, states


def topk_feat(logits):
    tv, ti = torch.topk(logits, TOPK, dim=-1)
    lse = torch.logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)
    return tv, ti, lse


def shadow_of(eng, states, rows):
    """Per-layer top-k / logsumexp at the given positions, from the layer-output
    boundary states (states[2l+2] = output of layer l)."""
    tvs, tis, lses = [], [], []
    for l in range(eng.L):
        lg = eng.logits(states[2 * l + 2][:, rows])[0]
        tv, ti, lse = topk_feat(lg)
        tvs.append(tv)
        tis.append(ti)
        lses.append(lse)
    return (torch.stack(tvs).to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy(),
            torch.stack(tis).to(torch.int32).cpu().numpy(),
            torch.stack(lses).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ decoding
class Decoder:
    def __init__(self, eng, eos_ids, rule):
        self.eng = eng
        self.eos = set(int(e) for e in eos_ids)
        self.rule = rule
        self.full = np.ones(2 * eng.L, dtype=bool)
        self.keep_states = False

    # ---- controller round trip with metered services
    def ask(self, header, arrays=None):
        self.rule.send(header, arrays)
        while True:
            h, a = self.rule.recv()
            t = h.get("type")
            if t == "probe":
                self.serve_probe(h, a)
            elif t == "apply":
                self.serve_apply(h, a)
            elif t == "states":
                self.serve_states(h)
            elif t == "head":
                self.serve_head(a)
            elif t == "ans":
                return h, a
            else:
                raise ProtocolError("unexpected frame %r from the draft controller" % t)

    def serve_probe(self, h, a):
        """Run a candidate draft over committed generated tokens [i0, i1) (indices
        into this prompt's generated tokens), teacher-forced, attending to the
        committed cache before them; return each position's draft top-k."""
        keep = self._mask(a.get("mask"))
        i0, i1 = int(h.get("i0", -1)), int(h.get("i1", -1))
        n_gen = len(self.gen)
        if not (0 <= i0 < i1 <= n_gen - 1) or i1 - i0 > MAX_PROBE_TOK:
            raise ProtocolError("probe range out of bounds")
        p0 = self.T + i0
        toks = torch.tensor([self.gen[i0:i1]], device="cuda")
        pos = torch.arange(p0, p0 + (i1 - i0), device="cuda")
        hh = self.eng.emb(toks)
        out, _ = self.eng.run(hh, pos, keep, ctx=p0, write_at=None)
        tv, ti, lse = topk_feat(self.eng.logits(out)[0])
        self.cost += float(self.eng.sub_cost[keep].sum())
        self.n_probe += 1
        self.rule.send({"type": "probe_result"},
                       {"top_val": tv.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy(),
                        "top_id": ti.to(torch.int32).cpu().numpy(),
                        "lse": lse.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)})

    def serve_apply(self, h, a):
        """Apply sublayer b to controller-supplied states X (nb, n, d): each of the
        nb branches is a copy of the LAST n committed positions, attending to the
        committed cache before them and causally to its own branch."""
        b = int(h.get("block", -1))
        n = int(h.get("n", 0))
        X = a.get("x")
        if not (0 <= b < 2 * self.eng.L) or X is None or X.ndim != 3:
            raise ProtocolError("bad apply request")
        nb, nn, d = X.shape
        if nn != n or n < 1 or n > min(RECENT, self.clen - self.T + 1) or d != self.d \
                or nb * n > MAX_APPLY_ROWS:
            raise ProtocolError("bad apply shape")
        x = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float32)).to("cuda", self.eng.dtype).reshape(1, nb * n, d)
        l = b // 2
        if b % 2 == 0:
            ctx = self.clen - n
            pos = torch.arange(ctx, ctx + n, device="cuda").repeat(nb)
            blk = torch.block_diag(*[torch.tril(torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"))] * nb)
            y = self.eng.attn(l, x, self.eng.rope(x, pos), ctx, None, blk)
        else:
            y = self.eng.mlp(l, x)
        self.cost += float(self.eng.sub_cost[b])
        self.n_apply += 1
        self.rule.send({"type": "apply_result"},
                       {"y": y.reshape(nb, n, d).to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy()})

    def serve_states(self, h):
        n = int(h.get("n", 0))
        have = len(self.recent)
        if not self.keep_states or not (1 <= n <= have):
            raise ProtocolError("states: %d requested, %d kept (keep_states must be set)" % (n, have))
        st = torch.stack(self.recent[-n:], 1)   # (2L+1, n, d)
        self.rule.send({"type": "states_result"}, {"x": st.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy()})

    def serve_head(self, a):
        X = a.get("x")
        if X is None or X.ndim != 2 or X.shape[1] != self.d or X.shape[0] > MAX_APPLY_ROWS:
            raise ProtocolError("bad head request")
        x = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float32)).to("cuda", self.eng.dtype)[None]
        tv, ti, lse = topk_feat(self.eng.logits(x)[0])
        self.rule.send({"type": "head_result"},
                       {"top_val": tv.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy(),
                        "top_id": ti.to(torch.int32).cpu().numpy(),
                        "lse": lse.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)})

    def _mask(self, m):
        if m is None:
            raise ProtocolError("missing sublayer mask")
        m = np.asarray(m).astype(bool).reshape(-1)
        if m.shape[0] != 2 * self.eng.L or not m.any():
            raise ProtocolError("draft mask must have 2L entries with at least one kept sublayer")
        return m

    def _plan(self, h, a):
        if "exit" in h:
            E = int(h["exit"])
            if not (1 <= E <= self.eng.L):
                raise ProtocolError("exit layer out of range")
            keep = np.zeros(2 * self.eng.L, dtype=bool)
            keep[:2 * E] = True
        else:
            keep = self._mask(a.get("mask"))
        g = int(h.get("max_draft", 0))
        if g < 0:
            raise ProtocolError("negative max_draft")
        return keep, min(g, MAX_DRAFT), bool(h.get("feedback", False)), bool(h.get("tree", False))

    # ---- one prompt
    @torch.no_grad()
    def prompt(self, ids, max_new, seq):
        eng = self.eng
        T = len(ids)
        self.T, self.d = T, eng.m.config.hidden_size
        self.recent = []
        self.cost = 0.0
        self.n_probe = self.n_apply = 0
        rounds = drafted = accepted = 0
        x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda")
        out, st = eng.run(eng.emb(x), torch.arange(T, device="cuda"), self.full, ctx=0, write_at=0,
                          collect=True)
        first = int(eng.logits(out[:, -1:])[0, 0].argmax())
        self.cost += eng.L
        rows = torch.arange(max(0, T - PREFILL_SHADOW), T, device="cuda")
        sv, si, sl = shadow_of(eng, st, rows)
        del st, out
        self.clen = T
        self.gen = [first]
        cur = first
        done = first in self.eos
        self.rule.send({"type": "begin", "seq": int(seq), "prompt_len": T},
                       {"shadow_val": sv, "shadow_id": si, "shadow_lse": sl,
                        "context": np.asarray(ids[-PREFILL_SHADOW:] + [first], dtype=np.int64)})
        while not done and len(self.gen) < max_new:
            h, a = self.ask({"type": "plan", "n_gen": len(self.gen)})
            keep, g, feedback, tree = self._plan(h, a)
            if h.get("keep_states"):
                self.keep_states = True
            g = min(g, max_new - len(self.gen) - 1)
            dcost = float(eng.sub_cost[keep].sum())
            drafts, s_tv, s_ti, s_lse = [], [], [], []
            tok = cur
            for i in range(g):
                hh = eng.emb(torch.tensor([[tok]], device="cuda"))
                o, _ = eng.run(hh, torch.tensor([self.clen + i], device="cuda"), keep,
                               ctx=self.clen + i, write_at=self.clen + i)
                tv, ti, lse = topk_feat(eng.logits(o)[0])
                self.cost += dcost
                tok = int(ti[0, 0])
                drafts.append(tok)
                s_tv.append(tv[0]); s_ti.append(ti[0]); s_lse.append(lse[0])
                if tok in self.eos:
                    break
                if feedback and i + 1 < g:
                    fh, _ = self.ask({"type": "step", "i": i},
                                     {"top_val": tv.to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy(),
                                      "top_id": ti.to(torch.int32).cpu().numpy(),
                                      "lse": lse.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)})
                    if not fh.get("cont", False):
                        break
            nodes_par, nodes_tok = None, None
            if tree and drafts:
                th, ta = self.ask({"type": "tree", "n": len(drafts)},
                                  {"top_val": torch.stack(s_tv).to(torch.float16).cpu().numpy(),
                                   "top_id": torch.stack(s_ti).to(torch.int32).cpu().numpy(),
                                   "lse": torch.stack(s_lse).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)})
                nodes_par = np.asarray(ta.get("parent"), dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1)
                nodes_tok = np.asarray(ta.get("token"), dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1)
                if nodes_par.shape != nodes_tok.shape or not (1 <= nodes_par.size <= MAX_TREE) \
                        or np.any(nodes_par >= np.arange(nodes_par.size)) or np.any(nodes_par < -1) \
                        or np.any(nodes_tok < 0) or np.any(nodes_tok >= eng.head.out_features):
                    raise ProtocolError("malformed draft tree (parents must precede children)")
                # every tree token is a DRAFT proposal: a node at depth k must be one of
                # the top-k tokens of draft step k-1 (the tree is built from the draft
                # distributions, as in SWIFT; tokens from elsewhere are not drafts)
                cand = torch.stack(s_ti).cpu().numpy()
                ndep = np.zeros(nodes_par.size, dtype=np.int64)
                for j in range(nodes_par.size):
                    ndep[j] = 1 if nodes_par[j] < 0 else ndep[nodes_par[j]] + 1
                    if ndep[j] > len(drafts) or nodes_tok[j] not in cand[ndep[j] - 1]:
                        raise ProtocolError("tree node %d is not a top-%d token of draft step %d"
                                            % (j, TOPK, ndep[j] - 1))
            # ---- verification: the full model over [cur] + drafts (chain) or [cur] + tree
            if nodes_par is None:
                q_tok = [cur] + drafts
                q = len(q_tok)
                pos = torch.arange(self.clen, self.clen + q, device="cuda")
                qmask = None
            else:
                q_tok = [cur] + nodes_tok.tolist()
                q = len(q_tok)
                par = np.concatenate([[-1], nodes_par + 1])   # node i+1's parent row
                depth = np.zeros(q, dtype=np.int64)
                anc = np.zeros((q, q), dtype=bool)
                anc[0, 0] = True
                for j in range(1, q):
                    pj = int(par[j]) if par[j] >= 0 else 0
                    depth[j] = depth[pj] + 1
                    anc[j] = anc[pj]
                    anc[j, j] = True
                pos = torch.as_tensor(self.clen + depth, device="cuda")
                qmask = torch.as_tensor(anc, device="cuda")
            hh = eng.emb(torch.tensor([q_tok], device="cuda"))
            o, st = eng.run(hh, pos, self.full, ctx=self.clen, write_at=self.clen, qmask=qmask,
                            collect=True)
            tgt = eng.logits(o)[0].argmax(-1).tolist()   # the full model's greedy choice per row
            self.cost += eng.L
            if nodes_par is None:
                n = 0
                while n < len(drafts) and drafts[n] == tgt[n]:
                    n += 1
                path = list(range(n + 1))       # rows committed: cur + accepted drafts
            else:
                path, r = [0], 0
                while True:
                    kids = [j for j in range(1, q) if (par[j] if par[j] >= 0 else 0) == r
                            and j != 0 and q_tok[j] == tgt[r]]
                    if not kids:
                        break
                    r = kids[0]
                    path.append(r)
                n = len(path) - 1
                if path != list(range(len(path))):
                    rows_t = torch.as_tensor(path, device="cuda")
                    for l in range(eng.L):     # move the accepted path's K/V to contiguous slots
                        eng.K[l, :, :, self.clen:self.clen + len(path)] = \
                            eng.K[l, :, :, self.clen + rows_t].clone()
                        eng.V[l, :, :, self.clen:self.clen + len(path)] = \
                            eng.V[l, :, :, self.clen + rows_t].clone()
            new = [q_tok[j] for j in path[1:]] + [tgt[path[-1]]]
            # structural greedy-equivalence: each emitted token is the full model's
            # argmax at the row of its predecessor
            assert all(new[k] == tgt[path[k]] for k in range(len(new)))
            rows = torch.as_tensor(path if nodes_par is not None else list(range(q)), device="cuda")
            sv, si, sl = shadow_of(eng, st, rows)
            if self.keep_states:
                prow = torch.as_tensor(path, device="cuda")
                for k in range(len(path)):
                    self.recent.append(torch.stack([s[0, prow[k]] for s in st]))
                self.recent = self.recent[-RECENT:]
            del st, o
            self.clen += len(path)
            rounds += 1
            drafted += len(drafts)
            accepted += n
            room = max_new - len(self.gen)
            new = new[:room]
            emitted = []
            for t in new:
                self.gen.append(t)
                emitted.append(t)
                if t in self.eos:
                    done = True
                    break
            cur = self.gen[-1]
            self.rule.send({"type": "result", "accepted": n, "n_draft": len(drafts),
                            "tree": nodes_par is not None},
                           {"draft": np.asarray(drafts, dtype=np.int64),
                            "tokens": np.asarray(emitted, dtype=np.int64),

"""Score spec for llm-early-exit-criterion (lossless self-speculative decoding).

Objective per setting: `etpl` -- generated tokens per unit of decoder parameters
loaded (one unit = one decoder layer), per prompt, averaged over prompts (DEL's
empirical token-per-layer, arXiv:2504.05598).  Higher is better; it has no
useful theoretical bound, so each term is a sigmoid anchored on the measured
baselines (weakest -> 0, strongest -> ref_score).  The output text is the full
model's greedy decoding whatever the controller does (the decoder verifies
every token), so there is no quality term.  All other columns are diagnostics.

for _s in ("set_a", "set_b", "set_c", "set_d"):
    term("etpl_%s" % _s, col("etpl_%s" % _s).higher().id().sigmoid())
    setting(_s, weighted_mean(("etpl_%s" % _s, 1.0)))

#!/bin/bash
# llm-early-exit-criterion -- shared driver for every setting (sourced by set_*.sh).
#
# Process split:
#   ee_decode.py    root, isolated interpreter, run from an immutable sha-checked
#                   COPY of the harness taken before any candidate code runs.
#                   Owns the model and the prompts; runs lossless
#                   self-speculative greedy decoding, verifies every drafted
#                   token with the full model, counts the cost and scores.
#   rule_server.py  unprivileged uid 1701, CPU only, spawned by the decoder behind
#                   a framed pipe protocol.  Imports the candidate draft_policy.py.
#
# The single scored line is relayed from this shell after every Python process
# has exited, followed by MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK as the very last line.
set -euo pipefail

: "${LABEL:?}" "${MODEL:?}" "${PROMPTS:?}" "${N_LAYERS:?}"
SEED="${SEED:-42}"
N_SCORED="${N_SCORED:-500}"
N_CAL=192
MAX_NEW=512
MAX_RULE_BYTES=32768
RUNUID=1701
RUNGID=1701
DATA=/data/layerskip-gen

WS=/workspace/layerskip-ee-lab/mlsee
OUT="${OUTPUT_DIR:-/tmp/ee_out}/${LABEL}-${SEED}"

if [ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: this evaluation drops privileges to keep the model, the prompts and the references out of the candidate process and therefore needs a root container\n'
    exit 1
fi
if [ ! -d "$DATA" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: %s is missing from the image\n' "$DATA"
    exit 1
fi
# The scored test prompts and their references are NOT in the image: they are
# verifier-only (holdout -> tests/meta/data/, reached through MLSBENCH_TASK_DIR
# at evaluation time).  EE_SCORED_DIR overrides for local development.
# The file names are spelled out: the verifier exports a holdout file into the
# eval-time task copy only when an eval script names it.
case "$PROMPTS" in
    cnndm.json) SCORED_FILE=cnndm_scored.json.gz ;;
    xsum.json)  SCORED_FILE=xsum_scored.json.gz ;;
    *)          SCORED_FILE="${PROMPTS%.json}_scored.json.gz" ;;
esac
SCORED=""
for d in "${MLSBENCH_TASK_DIR:-/nonexistent}/data" "${EE_SCORED_DIR:-}"; do
    if [ -n "$d" ] && [ -f "$d/$SCORED_FILE" ]; then SCORED="$d/$SCORED_FILE"; break; fi
done
if [ -z "$SCORED" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: the scored prompt file %s is not available to the evaluator\n' "$SCORED_FILE"
    exit 1
fi
# The model and the calibration prompts are readable by root only.
chown -R 0:0 "$DATA" 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 700 "$DATA"
# ...and must be byte-identical to what was measured: the agent phase runs as
# root in this image, so a modified weight or tokenizer file (or an added one,
# e.g. added_tokens.json) would change what is being scored.  Exactly the pinned
# files, each with its pinned sha256.
SUMS="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/data_sha256.txt"
want=$(awk -v m="$MODEL/" -v p="prompts/$PROMPTS" 'index($2, m) == 1 || $2 == p' "$SUMS")
have=$(cd "$DATA" && { find "$MODEL" -type f ! -path '*/original/*' ! -name '*.md' ! -name 'LICENSE*'; echo "prompts/$PROMPTS"; } | sort)
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$want" | awk '{print $2}' | sort)" != "$have" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: %s/%s does not hold exactly the pinned files\n' "$DATA" "$MODEL"
    exit 1
fi
if ! (cd "$DATA" && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c -); then
    printf 'INVALID: a baked model or prompt file does not match its pinned sha256\n'
    exit 1
fi

rm -rf "$OUT"
mkdir -p "$OUT/work"
chmod 755 "$OUT"
if [ -n "${MLSBENCH_RUN_UNTRUSTED:-}" ]; then
    chmod 755 "$OUT/work"          # the run-untrusted helper hands it to its fresh uid
else
    chown "$RUNUID:$RUNGID" "$OUT/work"
    chmod 700 "$OUT/work"
fi
find "$WS" -maxdepth 2 -name '__pycache__' -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
find "$WS" -maxdepth 2 -name '*.pyc' -delete 2>/dev/null || true

HARNESS=$(mktemp -d)
# The rule process must not reach the GPU: device nodes are closed to other
# uids for the duration of the eval (root, i.e. the decoder, keeps access).
NVMODES=""
for f in /dev/nvidia*; do
    if [ -c "$f" ]; then NVMODES="$NVMODES$(stat -c '%a %n' "$f")"$'\n'; chmod 0660 "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; fi

# where the runtime maps the device nodes to an unowned uid, e.g. userns docker).
if /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid="$RUNUID" --regid="$RUNGID" --clear-groups \
        /bin/sh -c 'for f in /dev/nvidiactl /dev/nvidia[0-9]*; do [ -e "$f" ] && [ -r "$f" ] && exit 0; done; exit 1'; then
    GPU_CLOSED=0
else
    GPU_CLOSED=1
fi
cleanup() {
    printf '%s' "$NVMODES" | while read -r m f; do if [ -n "$f" ]; then chmod "$m" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; done || true
    pkill -9 -u "$RUNUID" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -rf "$HARNESS" "$OUT"

# the agent phase): they come from the task's own read-only meta directory
# (tests/meta/edits in Harbor, the task dir natively), are copied into a fresh
# root-owned 0755 dir, and must match the digests pinned in harness_sha256.txt
# (which lives beside this script, outside /workspace).  The copies in
# /workspace/layerskip-ee-lab/mlsee/ are reading material only.

    printf 'INVALID: trusted harness sources not found outside /workspace\n'
    exit 1
fi
case "$TRUST_SRC" in /workspace/layerskip-ee-lab/*) printf 'INVALID: trusted harness under the writable workspace\n'; exit 1;; esac
cp "$TRUST_SRC/harness_decode.py" "$HARNESS/ee_decode.py"
cp "$TRUST_SRC/harness_rule_server.py" "$HARNESS/rule_server.py"
chown -R 0:0 "$HARNESS"
chmod 755 "$HARNESS"
chmod 644 "$HARNESS"/*.py
PINS="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/harness_sha256.txt"
SHA_DEC=$(awk '$2=="harness_decode.py"{print $1}' "$PINS")
SHA_SRV=$(awk '$2=="harness_rule_server.py"{print $1}' "$PINS")

rule_bytes=$(stat -c %s "$WS/draft_policy.py")
if [ "$rule_bytes" -gt "$MAX_RULE_BYTES" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: draft_policy.py is %d bytes, over the %d byte limit for this file\n' \
        "$rule_bytes" "$MAX_RULE_BYTES"
    exit 1

cp "$WS/draft_policy.py" "$OUT/work/draft_policy.py"
chmod 644 "$OUT/work/draft_policy.py"

PY=""
for p in /opt/conda/bin/python3 /usr/local/bin/python3 /usr/bin/python3; do
    if [ -x "$p" ]; then PY="$p"; break; fi
done
# The exit rule (untrusted) runs in its own process, spawned by the decoder:
#  * Harbor: through the verifier's $MLSBENCH_RUN_UNTRUSTED helper (fresh uid,
#    no inherited fds, its output relayed minus metric markers, every process of
#    the uid killed when it exits; the call is recorded next to the result file);
#  * natively: /usr/bin/setpriv to uid 1701 with no caps and no new privileges.
if [ -n "${MLSBENCH_RUN_UNTRUSTED:-}" ]; then
    read -r -a RU <<< "$MLSBENCH_RUN_UNTRUSTED"
    RULE_CMD=$("$PY" -I -S -c 'import json, sys
print(json.dumps({"mode": "helper",
                  "prefix": sys.argv[1:-4] + ["--writable", sys.argv[-4],
                                              "--strip", "^\\s*(FINAL_)?TEST_METRICS:",
                                              "--strip", "^\\s*MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK"],
                  "cmd": [sys.argv[-3], "-B", "-s", sys.argv[-2], sys.argv[-1]]}))' \
        "${RU[@]}" "$OUT/work" "$PY" "$HARNESS/rule_server.py" "$OUT/work/draft_policy.py")

        "$RUNUID" "$RUNGID" "$PY" "$HARNESS/rule_server.py" "$OUT/work/draft_policy.py")
fi

# The trusted root decoder starts through Harbor's hardened launcher
# ($MLSBENCH_TRUSTED_PYTHON: -I -S -B, no site hooks, no PYTHON* env, genuine
# site-packages appended; site-packages verified against the baked site
# manifest before the evals).  Natively: -I -S -B with the site dirs appended.
if [ -n "${MLSBENCH_TRUSTED_PYTHON:-}" ]; then
    read -r -a TPY <<< "$MLSBENCH_TRUSTED_PYTHON"
else
    TPY=("$PY" -I -S -B -c 'import sys, sysconfig, runpy
for k in ("purelib", "platlib"):
    p = sysconfig.get_path(k)
    if p not in sys.path: sys.path.append(p)

fi

STRIP='/^[[:space:]]*TEST_METRICS:/d; /^[[:space:]]*FINAL_TEST_METRICS:/d; /^[[:space:]]*MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK[[:space:]]*$/d'

if [ "$(sha256sum "$HARNESS/ee_decode.py" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "$SHA_DEC" ] \
   || [ "$(sha256sum "$HARNESS/rule_server.py" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "$SHA_SRV" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: the trusted harness does not match its pinned digest\n'
    exit 1
fi
set +e
dec_out=$(cd "$OUT" && "${TPY[@]}" "$HARNESS/ee_decode.py" \
    --model "$DATA/$MODEL" --prompts "$DATA/prompts/$PROMPTS" --scored "$SCORED" --workdir "$OUT/work" \
    --max-new "$MAX_NEW" \
    --n-scored "$N_SCORED" --n-cal "$N_CAL" --expect-layers "$N_LAYERS" \
    --rule-cmd "$RULE_CMD" --seed "$SEED" 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
pkill -9 -u "$RUNUID" 2>/dev/null || true
printf 'TRAIN_METRICS: gpu_closed_to_rule=%s\n' "$GPU_CLOSED"
printf '%s\n' "$dec_out" | grep -v -E 'past_key_values|Loading checkpoint|torch_dtype' | sed "$STRIP"
if [ -s "$OUT/rule.stderr" ]; then
    printf -- '--- draft_policy output (tail) ---\n'
    tail -n 30 "$OUT/rule.stderr" | sed "$STRIP"

if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then printf 'INVALID: expected exactly one TEST_METRICS line (found %s)\n' "$count"; exit 1; fi
FINAL=$(printf '%s\n' "$dec_out" | awk '/^TEST_METRICS:/ {sub(/^TEST_METRICS:/, "FINAL_TEST_METRICS:"); print}')

if [ -n "${MLSBENCH_RESULT_FILE:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$FINAL" 'MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK' >> "$MLSBENCH_RESULT_FILE"
